name: Péter Magyar
role: Hungarian prime minister since May 2026; Tisza party leader since 2024; MEP 2024-2026
summary: Magyar leads the Tisza party, which won a two-thirds majority in the April 2026 election. He campaigned on ending corruption, recovering frozen EU funds, restoring checks and balances and public services, while keeping Orbán-era border fence and a strict line on illegal migration. He calls himself a critical pro-European, backs NATO and eventual euro adoption, and avoided culture-war issues, though his government later moved to ease some LGBT restrictions.

notes:
Press reports of the Tisza programme (s2, s3, s13, s14) were used because the 240-page document itself could not be downloaded; they are classed as program sources. Several outlets (Telex, Intellinews, Politico) returned 403 or were not opened. He avoided questions on same-sex marriage, the death penalty and Pride policy; those stay null. Most recent positions (2026) are used where earlier ones differ, e.g. on Ukraine.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 33 answers taken from it, 24 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; earlier audit consulted only for notes and bibliography. The complete Hungarian-language 243-page TISZA programme was downloaded and searched, including all themes and the full blank list. Concise page locators refer to the printed page numbers, which match PDF page indices. Programme pledges are medium confidence, not proven outcomes. September parliamentary implementation claims are likewise medium unless independently established; the October AP interview and October 23 speech update earlier positions. The call for peaceful electoral change now does not negate his explicit approval of the 1956 uprising. Nine of the ten priority questions stay null. Anti-corruption rhetoric does not establish a Marxist theory of class history or exploitation. AI assistants supporting officials do not imply algorithms should take over government decision-making. General religious freedom does not answer the source of political authority. No inference from his former party or ideological labels.

claude-sonnet-5-5 later pass (2026-11-16): brought to rules 7 (sources tagged action or words; every statement answered, candidates included). The Hungarian 243-page programme was re-downloaded into the local library and searched by keyword for jury trial, central bank, dual citizenship, party financing, tax havens, torture, marriage, free trade, genocide denial, voting age, patents, migrant turn-backs, climate and platform regulation; only dual citizenship settled a new statement and the rest stay null. No earlier answer was changed.
